body: Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes is Capybara Games' Nintendo DS role-playing adventure built around tactical battles between grids of soldiers. Heroes from different factions explore the world of Ashan, recruit forces and pursue connected stories, with each confrontation asking the player to arrange units into useful formations. Matching pieces prepares attacks that will travel toward the opposing side after a delay. The army is therefore both a collection of characters and a puzzle surface, where moving one soldier can help prepare a larger action several turns before it actually happens.

A turn provides a limited number of moves for shifting units and forming groups of the same colour. A completed vertical formation begins charging, announcing an attack that the opponent can try to interrupt before it launches. Its path then interacts with the units standing between it and the enemy hero. The waiting period makes prediction important. Preparing a powerful action can create pressure, but the formation must survive long enough to deliver it, giving the opponent a visible problem and a chance to respond before the damage arrives.

Each faction supplies basic troops alongside larger advanced units, and the available selection shapes how its army can be assembled. Heroes gain experience and abilities through exploration and battles, while equipment can modify what the army or its leader can do. Multiplayer provides another setting in which to test those arrangements against a human opponent. The puzzle rules remain readable across the different forces, allowing the wider adventure to introduce new capabilities without abandoning the central question of which formation should be prepared now and whether it can remain intact until its turn arrives.
